claim: A game-agnostic online learner can conserve reliable mechanics across progressive levels, identify prediction residuals, localize new mechanics at the smallest useful causal layer, and reduce unnecessary exploratory actions without using game-specific solutions or exhaustive interaction search.

hypotheses.H1_transfer: Cross-level mechanic persistence reduces later-level exploratory actions versus per-level reset without reducing completion.
hypotheses.H2_conservative_repair: Local modifiers preserve still-correct base mechanics more often than they trigger global foundational rewrites.
hypotheses.H3_layer_relevance: CLEF relevance and stopping reduce redundant probes or representational expansion versus BLA-only without reducing completion or worsening action efficiency.

decision_rules.H1: paired median later-level exploratory actions for full persistence is strictly lower than per-level reset; completion count is not lower on more than 1 of 30 seeds in any family and aggregate completion is not lower
decision_rules.H2: in every required local-modifier adversarial family, still-correct base consequences remain active; aggregate erroneous global reopenings are lower than local scoped revisions
decision_rules.H3: full BLA+CLEF has strictly lower paired median redundant probes or active representational pressure than BLA-only; aggregate completions are not lower and median total actions do not increase by more than 5 percent
decision_rules.synthetic_confirmation: all hidden-boundary, receipt, replay, bounded-mode, package, protected-regression, source, secret, lint, format, type, and full-test gates pass in addition to H1-H3
decision_rules.real_completion: only the target official environment returning GameState.WIN

reporting.surface: synthetic for curriculum; local-public-source-preview-exposed for target play
